title: a run of test_the_seal_announces_itself leaves no _delivery table behind
intention: One run of cairn/devices/tester/proofs/test_the_seal_announces_itself.py leaves the database exactly as it found it: every table its fixture buses mint, delivery companions included, is gone when the run ends, and a new tooth reads the database to say so.
why: Measured 2026-11-14 on akiendell's cairn database: 24 tables named seal_ann_<pid>_<n>_delivery stand, owner bus, 0 rows, no cairn_scratch row, and their transit tables (seal_ann_<pid>_<n>) are gone. REPRODUCED ON DEMAND: one run of the proof (venv python, bare) took the count from 21 to 24, three leaked _delivery tables per run, which is the three fixture buses its teeth open (_fixture_bus -> scratch_bus('seal_ann')). A plain scratch_bus used and exited leaks nothing (measured: bus._ensure() and a post, then the exit: zero tables left), so the leak is specific to how this proof uses the bus. The same class was measured on 2026-09-06 (2,424 orphan _delivery tables, ticket 201a37bf1613, whose fix registers the companion at _ensure); this is a path that fix does not reach. Nothing in the proof reads the database after itself, so nothing noticed for as many runs as the 24 tables.
traces_to: Law 4 (a proof must not outlive its run: the scratch door exists for this), Law 9 (a green proof that litters the database is green over a leak).
how: Step 1, the bisect, recorded in the ticket's measured: run each tooth alone and list seal_ann_* before and after, to find which fixture path creates a _delivery table that is never registered as a scratch companion (candidates: the CLI child's own BusDevice on the same table name running _ensure after the parent's family is dropped; _SCRATCH never closed; the tell path). Step 2, the fix where the bisect lands: in the proof's fixture if it is the fixture (the bus is entered and closed per tooth, and the child never holds the table past it); the ticket is split into the store or the bus's own ticket if the bisect lands there, per RULE 1. Step 3, a new proof with one tooth that counts tables named seal_ann_% before and after one run of the leaking proof's three fixture shapes, and asserts the difference is zero. Red-first: the tooth reds today with a difference of 3.
